submitted.rationale: Index 3 (Bi0.10 Cu0.15 V0.75) had the highest measured photocurrent, 5.04e-6 A. That is about 4x the BiVO4-like point at index 293. The neighbouring V-rich point at index 42 gave a similar 4.89e-6 A, so the V-rich, low-Cu corner looks like the best region. The foundation-model receipts did not inform any choice: the phase list was too large to read, so I could not tie them to known phases.

rejected.reason: BiVO4-like, Bi:V near 1:1 with Cu 0.19; measured 1.24e-6 A, about 4x lower
V-rich neighbour of 3; measured 4.89e-6 A, slightly lower

consultations.verdict: Uninformative: the only valid receipt is a MEGNet HSE gap of 0.32 eV for mp-704645. I don't know that phase's formula because the phase list was too large to read. I am choosing 293 based on prior knowledge: with Bi:V near 1:1 and the lowest Cu, it is the composition closest to BiVO4, a known photoanode that absorbs at 3.2 eV.
Uninformative: this is a PBE gap for an unidentified phase. I am measuring 3 to explore the V-rich, low-Cu corner (likely BiVO4 plus V2O5 or CuV2O6) as a hedge against the BiVO4-like result at 293.

Uninformative: this is a SCAN gap for an unidentified phase. Measured data show the V-rich corner (index 3, 5.0 µA) beats the BiVO4-like point (index 293, 1.2 µA) by about 4x. Index 42 has the highest V fraction in the library, so I am using the last measurement on it.
